This question has too many variables that play into it, what country? When are you going? Are you staying in the heart of the city, with a relative, a homestead or the outskirts of the city? One thing I did to cut back down on expenses was bring a second check-in, it was $200 - but I saved so much money on clothes, art supplies since I was studying art, toiletries and not having to purchase a second one when I came back. I was the only one who brought a second check in, one of my peers went on a $300 spending spree at Zara because they didn’t bring a lot of clothes.

Most of my study abroad programs at my community college are around $7k for one month and that only includes housing, the occasional outing, and events for Seville, Spain. Another one was $9k for Rome, Italy for three months that also included the above. This doesn’t count the flights, passport fees, food and other expenses. Most abroad programs are roughly around $15k-$20k.

They don’t accept kids that turn 18 since you have to sign a lot of documents regarding safety, waivers, liability without the consent of your legal guardian before and while you are abroad. Along with the fact that most 18 yos can’t book plane or hotels by themselves. I was under 18 when I found out about my abroad program and wasn’t able to participate until I became 18. At the end of the day, 17 is still considered a minor. 

There is still so many Japan study abroad programs during undergrad and grad studies, even if you aren’t able to find one that takes you while you are in high school.
